method_card.title: Comparing Data Sets in Context
method_card.content:
Comparing two distributions requires two things: a comparison of central tendency (what is typical?) and a comparison of spread (how consistent?). Simply stating “A has a higher mean than B” is not enough — you must say what that means in the context of the question.

Which average to use?

  • Mean: best when data is roughly symmetrical and has no extreme outliers.
  • Median: better when data is skewed or has outliers (e.g. salaries, house prices).
  • Mode: useful for categorical data or when the most common value matters (e.g. shoe size).

Spread measures:

  • Range: simplest but affected by outliers. Foundation tier comparison measure.
  • Interquartile range (IQR = Q3 − Q1): more robust; not affected by outliers.
  • Standard deviation: Higher tier; measures average distance from the mean.

The spec is explicit: comparisons must be context-based interpretations, not just observations of numerical difference. A full comparison for 4 marks needs: (1) compare central tendency with a numerical value, (2) interpret what it means for the data subjects, (3) compare spread with a numerical value, (4) interpret what that means in context.
steps: Identify the two distributions to compare
Choose an appropriate measure of central tendency and calculate or read it off
Choose an appropriate measure of spread and calculate or read it off
Write a comparison sentence for central tendency that includes a number AND a context interpretation
Write a comparison sentence for spread that includes a number AND a context interpretation
Check: have you mentioned what the numbers mean for the people or things in the question?

exam_context.marks: Comparing distributions in context is typically 4 to 6 marks — the highest-mark question type per topic in this section
exam_context.frequency: Paper 2 almost always contains a compare-in-context question; it is the most frequently dropped mark block at GCSE level

worked_examples.question: The table below gives summary statistics for two class tests. A student says 'Class A did better.' Is this fully correct? Give a complete comparison of both distributions.

steps.label: Step 1 — Read the summary table
steps.content:
MeanRange
Class A148
Class B116

Class A has a higher mean (14 vs 11) but also a larger range (8 vs 6).

steps.label: Step 2 — Compare central tendency in context
steps.content: Class A has a higher mean (14 vs 11), which means on average Class A students scored 3 marks more than Class B students.

steps.label: Step 3 — Compare spread in context
steps.content: Class A has a larger range (8 vs 6), which means there is more variation in Class A's scores — the results are less consistent.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Class A did better on average (mean 14 compared to 11), but their scores were more spread out (range 8 compared to 6), suggesting Class A was less consistent than Class B.

worked_examples.question: The table below gives summary statistics for two basketball teams. Write a full comparison of the two distributions in context.

steps.label: Step 2 — Compare medians in context
steps.content: Team A has a higher median height (192 cm vs 185 cm), meaning the typical player in Team A is 7 cm taller than the typical player in Team B.

steps.label: Step 3 — Compare IQR in context
steps.content: Team A has a larger IQR (14 vs 8). This means there is more variation in the middle 50% of heights in Team A; their heights are more spread out than Team B's.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Team A's players are typically taller (median 192 cm vs 185 cm). However, Team B's heights are more consistent (IQR 8 vs 14), suggesting Team A's heights vary more between players.

worked_examples.question: The table below compares weekly wages at two companies. Both means are identical. What does the standard deviation tell us, and which company offers more consistent wages?

steps.label: Step 2 — Note the equal means
steps.content: Both companies pay workers an average of £420 per week, so central tendency alone does not distinguish them.

steps.label: Step 3 — Compare standard deviations in context
steps.content: Company A has a much higher standard deviation (£85 vs £30). This means wages in Company A are more spread out around the mean; individual wages vary more from worker to worker.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Company B offers more consistent wages. Although both companies pay the same average (£420), Company B's standard deviation is much lower (£30 vs £85), meaning workers in Company B are paid more similarly to one another. In Company A there is much greater variation in individual pay.

options: Set A, because its mean is higher
Set B, because its mean is lower
They are the same, because both ranges are equal
Set A, because a higher mean always means less spread

misconceptions.message: The mean measures the typical value. Set A's mean (25) is higher than Set B's mean (20). The range does not tell us about typical values.

bronze.display: Five daily temperatures (°C) for a week: 12, 15, 14, 11, 18. Calculate the range.

Salary
£18 000
£22 000
£24 000
£25 000
£95 000

Which average is most appropriate to represent the typical salary?
options: Median, because the extreme high value (£95 000) would distort the mean
Mean, because it uses all the values
Mode, because it is the most common value
Range, because it shows the spread

misconceptions.message: When there is an outlier (£95 000), the mean is pulled upward and becomes unrepresentative. The median is better because it is not affected by outliers.

Which group is faster on average?
options: Group A, because its median time is lower (faster)
Group B, because its median time is higher
Group A, because its range is larger
Group B, because its range is smaller

misconceptions.message: Lower time = faster. Group A's median (13.2 s) is lower than Group B's (14.1 s), so Group A is typically faster.

bronze.display: A data set has values: 5, 8, 8, 12, 17, 19, 23, 27. Find the median.

misconceptions.message: n = 8 (even). Median = mean of 4th and 5th values = (12 + 17) / 2 = 14.5.

bronze.display:
GroupMeanStandard deviation
Group X6012
Group Y604

Which group's data is more spread out?
options: Group X, because its standard deviation is larger
Group Y, because its standard deviation is smaller
Both groups, because the means are equal
Neither, because standard deviation measures central tendency

misconceptions.message: Standard deviation measures spread. A larger standard deviation means greater spread. Group X (SD = 12) is more spread out than Group Y (SD = 4).

bronze.display: A student writes: 'Team A scored more goals than Team B because Team A has a higher mean.' Identify the problem with this comparison statement.
options: It does not interpret the mean in context — it should say what a higher mean means for typical goal-scoring performance
The student should have compared ranges instead
The statement is correct and complete
The student should have used the mode instead of the mean

misconceptions.message: A context-based interpretation must go beyond the number. The student should add something like: 'meaning Team A typically scored more goals per game than Team B.'

silver.display:
Call centreMean complaints/dayIQR
Centre A187
Centre B224

Which statement is the best comparison of these distributions?
options: Centre A receives fewer complaints on average (mean 18 vs 22) and has more day-to-day variation in complaints (IQR 7 vs 4)
Centre B is better because it has a smaller IQR
Centre A is worse because it has a bigger IQR
The centres are similar because their means are close

misconceptions.message: A good comparison names both the measure, the values, and the real-world meaning. Option A correctly compares both central tendency and spread in context.

silver.display: Times (minutes) taken by 7 students to complete a puzzle: 8, 10, 11, 13, 15, 17, 22. Find Q1 and Q3. Give Q1 first.

misconceptions.message: n = 7 (one less than 8, a multiple of 4). Q1 is the 2nd value = 10. Q3 is the 6th value = 17.

silver.display:

Sample558
National population5214

What does the standard deviation comparison tell you about the sample vs population?
options: The sample's scores are more tightly clustered around the mean than the national population; less variation in the sample
The sample performed better because its mean is higher
The population is more reliable because its standard deviation is higher
Standard deviation cannot be compared across different-sized groups

misconceptions.message: A smaller standard deviation means less spread. The sample (SD 8) is more tightly clustered around its mean than the national population (SD 14), meaning there is less variation in the sample's scores.

Without calculating, which group has a larger range?
options: Group B, because its values spread from 180 to 260 (range 80)
Group A, because all values are larger
Group A, because they are more consistent
Group B, because its mean is lower

misconceptions.message: Range = max − min. Group A: 230 − 210 = 20. Group B: 260 − 180 = 80. Group B has the larger range.

School A45 min20 min

Which school's homework times are more consistent?
options: School A, because its IQR (20 min) is smaller than School B's (35 min), showing less variation in homework time
School B, because its IQR is larger, meaning more students are near the median
School A, because its median is higher
School B, because a larger IQR means more data is captured

misconceptions.message: Smaller IQR = more consistent middle 50%. School A's IQR (20 min) is smaller, meaning the middle half of students in School A are more similar in their homework time.

silver.display:
CityMean house price
City X£280 000
City Y£195 000

A developer says 'City X houses are always more expensive.' Explain why this claim might not be fully justified.
options: The mean is an average; individual prices in City Y might be higher than some in City X depending on spread
The mean is not a useful measure for house prices
The developer is correct — a higher mean always means every house is more expensive
Only the mode should be used for house prices

misconceptions.message: The mean tells us about typical values, not all values. With a large spread in City X, some houses there could be cheaper than houses in City Y.

gold.display:
TeamMean goals/matchStandard deviation
Team A2.40.6
Team B2.01.8

Write a complete comparison (4 marks). Which team would you recommend for consistent results?
options: Team A scores more on average (mean 2.4 vs 2.0) and is far more consistent (SD 0.6 vs 1.8), making Team A the more predictable, reliable scorer
Team B is better because higher standard deviation means more exciting matches
Team A is better only because of its higher mean — standard deviation is not relevant here
Both teams are similar because their means are close

misconceptions.message: A full comparison needs central tendency AND spread, both with context. Team A's lower SD means it consistently scores around 2.4 goals; Team B's high SD means its goal tally varies widely from match to match.

gold.display:
CompanyMedian weekly hoursIQR
Company A37 h6 h
Company B40 h22 h

A union says 'Company B workers work longer hours AND their hours are less predictable.' Is this justified?
options: Yes — Company B has a higher median (40 vs 37 hours) and a larger IQR (22 vs 6 hours), so workers there work more on average and hours vary more
No — the median cannot be used to compare working hours
No — the IQR only measures extreme values, not typical spread
Yes — but only the IQR comparison is valid; the medians cannot be compared

misconceptions.message: The union is correct. Median 40 > 37 (longer typical hours). IQR 22 > 6 (greater variation in hours — less predictable schedules).

gold.display:
CountryMean life expectancyRange
Country A74 years40 years
Country B68 years12 years

A researcher concludes 'Country A has better outcomes across all residents.' Give the best critique of this conclusion.
options: Country A's larger range (40 years vs 12 years) shows much greater inequality in outcomes; some residents may live far shorter lives despite the higher mean
Country A clearly has better outcomes — the mean is the only valid comparison measure here
Country B is better because its range is smaller, so the mean is irrelevant
Neither country can be compared without median data

misconceptions.message: A higher mean does not mean all residents have good outcomes. Country A's large range (40 years) suggests great inequality — some live very short lives even though the average is high.

gold.display:
HospitalMedian waiting timeIQR
Hospital A24 min8 min
Hospital B32 min30 min

Which statement gives the best 4-mark quality comparison?
options: Hospital A has shorter typical waiting times (median 24 vs 32 min) and its waiting times are more consistent (IQR 8 vs 30 min), meaning patients at Hospital A can better predict how long they will wait
Hospital A is better because the median is lower
Hospital B is worse only because of its higher median
Hospital A is better — the IQR shows Hospital B has more patients

misconceptions.message: A full 4-mark answer needs: numerical comparison of central tendency + context + numerical comparison of spread + context. Option A does all four elements.
